title: Relative rational maps on fibrewise dense opens
statement: Let $s_X:X\to S$ and $s_Y:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subseteq X$ is fibrewise dense if its inverse image in every fibre of $s_X$ is dense. A relative partial map is such an open together with a morphism $a:U\to Y$ satisfying $s_Y\circ a=s_X|_U$. Two partial maps are equivalent when they agree on a common fibrewise dense open contained in both domains. A relative rational map is an equivalence class for this relation. Its domain is the union of all its representative domains. A morphism on an open represents the class when its domain is fibrewise dense, it is over $S$, and its partial-map class is the given class. For $p:X\prime\to X$ over $S$, a class $\psi$ on $X\prime$ is the composite of $\phi$ with $p$ when, for every representative $a:U\to Y$ of $\phi$, the canonical composite $p^{-1}U\to U\to Y$ represents $\psi$ (so $p^{-1}U$ must be fibrewise dense).

source.place: BLR 2.5, printed p.55 (PDF p.61), definition of S-density and S-rational maps; p.57 maximal domain; Proposition 5 p.58 pullback representatives.
